title: Minimal models in numerical dimension one
main_claim: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n>=3 with K_X pseudo-effective and kappa_sigma(X,K_X)=1 (Nakayama's section-growth convention with a fixed ample twist). Then a finite K-MMP X --> Y reaches a Q-factorial terminal minimal model Y with K_Y nef. The proof uses positive-perturbation MMPs (BCHM), stabilization in codimension two, and a two-surface nefness criterion.

issues.description: The good-minimal-model corollary relies entirely on a companion paper's log abundance theorem for lc pairs (Y,0) with nef K_Y. That is the full abundance conjecture. The corollary is only as strong as that unaudited companion result. The main theorem does not depend on it.
issues.evidence: Apply the log abundance theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAILogAbundance2026} to the projective lc pair (Y,0)

coverage: I read all of paper.tex, introduction.tex, mmp.tex, numerics.tex and conclusion.tex, and checked each step of the main proof. (1) Lemma mmp:strict: the negativity-lemma argument and its support statement. (2) Lemma mmp:stabilization, both parts. The flipped-locus part: the blow-up valuation of a codimension-2 flipped component has a=2 on U_{i+1} and a<2 earlier, so it must be an original divisor that gets contracted, and each such divisor is used once. I sanity-checked this against 3-folds: there are no small K-negative contractions from smooth 3-folds. The flipping-locus part: the Borel-Moore localization argument gives dim A_d(U+) <= dim A_d(U), strictly when the flipping locus has a d-dimensional component. I checked the injectivity claim, which uses H_{2d}(Z+)=0. (3) Proposition mmp:approximation: the BCHM Cor 1.4.2 hypotheses (big boundary via the section injection, klt, nef start); the ray computation that each step is K-negative; the K-ampleness of the flipped side via K_U - bD being trivial over R; and the reflexive identification of sections across a codimension-3 isomorphism. (4) Lemma num:growth: the Nadel twist algebra (the residual is A_0+(r-i)A - m t_j pi*B_Y); the Koszul surjectivity; and the surface Riemann-Roch coefficients, which I recomputed. (5) Lemma num:jets: the principal-parts leading-jet argument and the degree bound b*g + deg >= 0. (6) Lemma num:fixed-square: the Hodge index bound on Q-perp, f*D.F=0 because F is f-exceptional, and the residual square >= 0. (7) Proposition num:nef: c is uniform in j, the surface through x meets the Z_j finitely, the component squares are nonnegative, and their sum tends to 0. (8) The transfer of quadratic growth back to X using u*K_X - r*pi*L >= 0 and the pushforward to P_X. I found no unjustified step. The cited results are applied within their hypotheses.
